This week, Apple launched a brand new rental program called Apple Upgrade, covering the vast majority of Apple products. The program completely replaces the iPhone Upgrade Program, and overall it's a very cost-effective choice.

This program is such a good deal that I basically can't find a strong reason to keep using Apple Card Monthly Installments (ACMI). Using Apple Upgrade also earns 3% cashback, similar to ACMI, but the rental terms are much more flexible than ACMI, and you don't have to rent forever. After the rental period ends, you can choose to buy the device, simply paying the difference between the rent you've already paid and the original price.

So this got me thinking — will Apple Card Monthly Installments be cancelled?

Apple Card transition to Chase

Earlier this year, Apple announced that the partner bank for Apple Card would change from Goldman Sachs to JPMorgan Chase. The transition isn't expected until early 2028, so there's still quite a while before any changes take place.

Although this isn't confirmation of any kind, Apple's wording on the Apple Card transition website doesn't seem very clear. Regarding the future of Apple Card Monthly Installments, the website says:

Apple used phrasing like "will be able to continue," and this kind of language doesn't inspire much confidence in the long-term survival of the program. Apple is only confirming that there won't be any changes in the short term.

Apple Upgrade

As I mentioned at the beginning, Apple Upgrade is a very cost-effective option that basically replaces the need to use Apple Card Monthly Installments. Apple Upgrade offers greater flexibility, longer repayment terms, and you can still earn 3% cashback through Apple Card — if you ultimately want to own the product, you can just buy it out without paying more than the original price.

That said, Apple Upgrade is launched in partnership with Klarna — and this raises a question: why not Chase? Since Chase is about to become the partner bank for Apple Card, why aren't they also providing support for this new rental program from Apple?

Put simply, I don't think this business has much profit margin. After all, there's no interest on financing, and no late fees — so for a major bank, the financial return is quite limited. Goldman Sachs has already experienced this firsthand.

If Chase won't support Apple Upgrade, they also might not support ACMI — so if that program eventually disappears, it wouldn't be too surprising. Apple Upgrade has largely replaced it; the only shortcoming is that a small number of products aren't included — but that can be adjusted in the future.

Of course, all of the above is purely speculation — but I think the timeline seems too obvious. I believe Apple Card Monthly Installments will continue to exist in the short term, but if Apple stops accepting new ACMI transactions at some point before 2028, I wouldn't be surprised at all.
